# About Me

I grew up between the UK and Nigeria, and my early experiences moving between different communities sparked a lasting curiosity about people, culture, and the worlds we create around us.

Growing up in Hackney, London, I became involved in youth advocacy and community building through organizations including **Hackney Youth Parliament**, **Hackney Quest**, and **Voyage Youth**. Through these experiences, I worked with young people on community projects, youth leadership, and creating spaces where young people could have a meaningful role in shaping their neighborhoods.

The arts have been a constant thread throughout my life. I began performing spoken word and poetry after winning the **Jack Petchey Speak Out Challenge**, and have continued writing and performing ever since. I have also been involved in theatre facilitation with **Limitless Theatre**, working with children with special needs, as well as community-based poetry and arts projects. In 2026, I received the **Elizabeth Babcock Poetry Prize** and the **Samuel A. Eliot Jr./Julia Heflin Award for Distinguished Directing in Theatre**.

I completed my bachelor degree at **Smith College**, where I studied Psychology and Theatre. Alongside my academic work, I became involved in suicide prevention and survivor advocacy. I continue to volunteer with **Impacted Survivors of Murder-Suicide**.

My education and experiences have taken me across several different cultural contexts. I have had the opportunity to study and live in places including **Barbados** and **Melbourne, Australia**, experiences that have broadened the way I think about culture, community, and human experience.

These different parts of my life: psychology; the arts; community work; and experiences across cultures continue to shape how I see the world and the questions I bring to my work.

When I'm not engaged in research or community building, you can usually find me doing something connected to the arts or movement. I love **dance, yoga, poetry, and theatre**, and I am happiest when I have opportunities to be creative. I also love to travel. One of my ongoing personal goals is to visit every continent. (I have **two more to go**.)

For me, travel, art, community work, and psychology are all connected by the same underlying curiosity: **people are complicated, creative, and shaped by the worlds around them.** I am interested in continuing to learn from those worlds, and in finding ways to contribute to them.
